stimulus.title: Surface tension of water with added detergent
stimulus.text: PLACEHOLDER content, written only to test the free-response pages; it has had no accuracy check. Students added different amounts of detergent to 100 mL of water at 20 °C and measured surface tension three times for each amount.

table.caption: Mean surface tension (± 2 SE) at each detergent concentration

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Describe one way the water molecules at the surface of the beaker interact with each other.

rubric.point: Surface water molecules form hydrogen bonds with the water molecules beside and below them (cohesion).
accept: hydrogen bonds hold surface molecules together

parts.sample: The water molecules at the surface form hydrogen bonds with neighboring molecules beside and below them, so they cling together.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in this investigation.

rubric.point: Independent: amount of detergent; dependent: surface tension (both needed).
accept: IV detergent drops, DV surface tension

parts.sample: The independent variable is the number of drops of detergent per 100 mL; the dependent variable is the surface tension of the water.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Construct a graph of the data, with the mean surface tension and error bars of ± 2 SE at each detergent concentration.

rubric.point: Correct axes: detergent on the x-axis, surface tension on the y-axis.

accept: mN/m and drops per 100 mL shown

rubric.point: All five means plotted correctly on a suitable scale.
Error bars of ± 2 SE drawn at every point.

parts.sample: A line graph with detergent (drops per 100 mL) on the x-axis from 0 to 8 and mean surface tension (mN/m) on the y-axis from 30 to 80, five points plotted at the means, each with an error bar extending 2 SE above and below, joined by straight lines.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Analyze the data to determine whether the surface tension at 6 drops differs from that at 8 drops. Justify your answer using the error bars.

rubric.point: States there is no clear (significant) difference between 6 and 8 drops.

parts.sample: There is no clear difference. The ± 2 SE ranges for 6 drops (39.0 to 41.4) and 8 drops (38.6 to 40.6) overlap, so the difference is likely due to chance.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Predict the surface tension at 12 drops of detergent, and justify your prediction.

rubric.point: Predicts about 39 to 40 mN/m, because surface tension levels off above 6 drops.
accept: close to 40 mN/m because the curve has leveled off

parts.sample: About 39 to 40 mN/m. The values stop falling after 6 drops, so adding more detergent should change little.
